text: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, Part II, if F is any antiderivative of a continuous function f on [a, b], then ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = ___.
explanation: FTC Part II states ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a): integrating the derivative recovers the net change. This is what makes integration practical, replacing limits of Riemann sums with evaluation of an antiderivative at the endpoints. The value is the difference of endpoint values in that order, not F(a) − F(b) nor an average.
